newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech money mkt feels effect of crown activity.
newsitem.headline: Czech money mkt feels effect of crown activity.

text.p: Czech crown one-year money market rates rose sharply on Thursday in a tumultuous day for the crown on the foreign exchange market which prompted central bank intervention.

Money market dealers said that one year rates had risen to around 12.30/12.60 percent from below 12 percent at the open although they stood a little below the highest rates of the day before the central bank intervened.

"People think the Czech crown could be lower so they sell it on spot...and in the meantime they find themselves short on Czech crowns for their general needs and this pushes the rate up," said one local dealer, explaining the knock on effect of the crown turmoil on the money market.
On Thursday morning, the central bank intervened to prop up the crown after the Czech currency slipped to minus five percent against the mid-point of its mark/dollar basket.
Following the intervention, the crown rebounded to minus 3.0 percent against the basket mid-point.

The central bank has said it would intervene further if necessary but on Thursday gave no indication it would raise interest rates to help the crown although last week it said it would if the need arose. The repo rate is 12.4 percent.
